chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Khazzāz, from ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn ʿAmr al-Khathʿamī, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said:
I said, “Is there a fixed time for this matter?” So he said, “The time-setters have lied, the time-setters have lied, the time-setters have lied.”

Indeed, when Mūsā (عليه السلام) went as a delegate to his Lord, he promised them thirty days; then when Allah added ten to the thirty, his people said, “Mūsā has broken his promise to us,” so they did what they did.

So when we narrate a hadith to you and it comes to pass in accordance with what we narrated to you, then say, “Allah has spoken the truth.” And when we narrate a hadith to you and it comes contrary to what we narrated to you, then say, “Allah has spoken the truth”; you will be rewarded twice.

key_terms.الْوَقَّاتُونَ: those who assign or specify a fixed time for an event
key_terms.صَدَقَ اللَّهُ: Allah has spoken the truth; an affirmation of divine truthfulness
key_terms.هَذَا الْأَمْرِ: this matter; the divinely ordained affair being asked about
key_terms.وَافِدًا: going as a delegate or one who comes in attendance

ai.seo_question: Does this hadith forbid specifying a set time for the appearance of Imam al-Mahdi (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith rejects setting a fixed time for the divinely ordained matter, condemning those who claim certainty about its timing. It draws on the account of Mūsā (عليه السلام) and his people to show how impatience and mistaken expectations lead people astray. It also teaches the believers to affirm Allah’s truthfulness and remain faithful even when events unfold differently from what they anticipated.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Khazzaz, from Abdul Kareem Bin Amro Al Khash’amy, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I said, ‘Is there a (specific) time for this matter?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The timers would be lying! The timers would be lying! The timers would be lying!

When (Prophet) Musa<sup>as</sup> went as a delegate to his<sup>as</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, his<sup>as</sup> appointment was for thirty days. So when Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Increased ten upon the thirty, his<sup>as</sup> people said, ‘Musa<sup>as</sup> has broken his<sup>as</sup> promise’. Thus, they did what they did.

So when we<sup>asws</sup> narrate to you all with the Hadeeth and there comes what we<sup>asws</sup> had narrated with, so you should be saying, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Spoke the truth’. And when we<sup>asws</sup> narrated to you all with the Hadeeth, so there comes different to what we<sup>asws</sup> had narrated to you with, so you should be saying, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Spoke the truth’. You would be Recompensed twice’.
en.sarwar: 5. Al-Husayn ibn mmd has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Khazzaz from ‘Abd al-Karim ibn ‘Umar al-Khath‘ami from al-Fadl ibn Yasar who has said the following. “I asked abu Ja’far (a.s.), ‘Is there a definite time for this matter (the rise of al-Mahdi with Divine Authority)?”
He said, “Those who set a definite time have lied, those who set a definite time have lied, those who set a definite time have lied.

When Musa (Moses) came out to delegate before his lord and gave the people a definite time for his return and Allah added an other ten days his people said, ‘He has broken his promise.’” They then did what they did.

When we say a hadith (make a statement to you) and if our hadith comes true you should say, “Allah has spoken the truth.” If we say a hadith to you ( make a statement) and if doe not come true, you should say, “Allah has spoken the truth.” You will be rewarded twice.”
